name: Emsculpt Neo
lead: Emsculpt Neo is a non-invasive body-contouring device made by BTL Industries that combines high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) energy, which causes strong muscle contractions, with radiofrequency (RF) heating of fat.[1][2] It is marketed for increasing muscle tone and reducing fat in areas such as the abdomen, buttocks, thighs and arms.

Systematic reviews published in 2023 to 2025 have examined the electromagnetic body-contouring literature and the HIFEM-plus-RF combination specifically.[3][4][5] Much of the research was manufacturer-linked device studies measured by imaging and photographs, and one review notes that all studies in its scope used the BTL device.[5]

paras: According to an AI-generated encyclopedia entry, the device sends alternating magnetic fields into tissue to stimulate motor neurons, producing contractions stronger than voluntary exercise, while synchronized RF energy heats subcutaneous fat.[1] That source reports a launch in 2020 as the successor of the original HIFEM-only Emsculpt introduced in 2018, and cites FDA clearances for abdominal lipolysis and for toning of the abdomen, buttocks, thighs, arms and calves, plus a 2024 rehabilitative clearance.[1] These details come from a source that may contain errors.

A 2023 systematic review in Annals of Plastic Surgery was described by its authors as the first to assess the efficacy and safety of electromagnetic body-contouring treatments, tabulating measurements from imaging studies.[3] A 2024 systematic review in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery examined HIFEM with and without RF for body contouring.[4] A 2025 review of electromagnetic treatment plus RF reported that seven studies measured fat and muscle thickness using ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging, and that all used the Emsculpt Neo device.[5]

The manufacturer-referenced figures repeated in one encyclopedia source are an average 25% increase in muscle and 30% fat reduction in treated areas.[1] Reviewers have noted that studies rely on photographs and imaging measurements in small samples.[3][5]
Separately, two registered trials started in December 2025 are testing BTL HIFEM-based devices for back pain, which is a medical rather than appearance use.[6][7]
The reviews above assessed safety alongside efficacy.[3][4] The manufacturer-based source describes no downtime and treatment suitable for patients with BMI up to 35.[1]
A manufacturer-derived source lists a 2019 FDA 510(k) clearance, a Health Canada license issued in 2020 and a CE mark.[1]

timeline.event: Original HIFEM-only Emsculpt introduced by BTL.[1]
Initial FDA 510(k) clearance reported for Emsculpt Neo.[1]
First systematic review of electromagnetic body-contouring treatments published.[3]
Systematic review of HIFEM with and without RF published.[4]

card.summary: A BTL machine that pairs electromagnetic muscle contractions with RF fat heating; reviews exist, but the studies largely use the same device.
card.note: Much of the published data uses the manufacturer's own device.

quick.overview:
Emsculpt Neo is a non-invasive contouring device that combines strong magnetic muscle contractions with radiofrequency heating of fat. It is marketed for toning and fat reduction on the abdomen, buttocks, thighs and arms.

Systematic reviews exist, though they describe small imaging-based studies, and the combination-device studies in one review all used the same device.
quick.mechanism: Alternating magnetic fields stimulate motor nerves to produce contractions stronger than voluntary exercise, while RF energy heats subcutaneous fat.
quick.risks: Reviews assessed safety alongside efficacy. The device is FDA-cleared for several body-contouring indications according to manufacturer-derived information; no long-term comparative data were located.
